question: By which name was the Head of the Panchayat or the Village Headman called in Mughal India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Muqaddam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In Mughal India, the head of the panchayat or the village headman was called the **Muqaddam**.
 
• The Muqaddam was responsible for maintaining law and order in the village and ensuring that the villagers adhered to the rules and regulations.
 
• The Muqaddam also played a vital role in the collection of taxes and ensuring that the revenue was appropriately managed and sent to the central authorities.
 
• They were often selected from the leading families of the village and were well-respected figures within their communities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Samant**

 
 
• Samants were feudal lords in medieval India who were granted land by the king in return for military support.
 
• They were responsible for the administration of their territories and for providing troops to the king when required.
 
 
 
• **Mahant**
 
 
• Mahants were religious leaders or heads of monasteries in India.
 
• They were responsible for the management of the monastery and the welfare of its inhabitants.
 
 
 
• **Khoran**
 
 
• The term "Khoran" does not have a significant historical reference in the context of village administration in Mughal India.
